<findings>
<finding task="3"><quote>R1.3 **`compatibility`.** When present, a string of 1–500 characters after stripping.</quote><plan>R1.3: `compatibility` is "a string of 1–500 UTF-8 bytes after stripping".</plan><fix>Quote R1.3 as the spec words it: "1–500 characters after stripping". In Task 3, measure `len(compat.strip())` in characters, not `.encode('utf-8')` bytes. Change the error message and the `COMPATIBILITY_CAP` comment to say characters. Add a multibyte test case, such as 500 copies of a non-ASCII character, that must pass. If the owner wants bytes, that is a spec-level change: it needs an amendment task and a D-line, and should not be presented as a verbatim copy.</fix></finding>
<finding task="7"><quote>CLAUDE.md's Commands section gains the `--strict` invocation with one line on when to use it (preparing a claude.ai upload or a spec-only validator run)</quote><plan>- **D7** (owner, plan review, 2026-10-18): Task 7 names `--strict` in the frontmatter lint's existing CLAUDE.md comment and adds no line. Applied in: Task 7.</plan><fix>D7 changes what R1.9 requires: the spec asks for the invocation itself, and the plan only puts a flag name in a comment. That makes it a spec-level decision. Add an amendment block for R1.9 to Task 1, tagged `(owner, plan 53, 2026-10-18)`, and log D7 as "Applied in: Task 1 (spec amendment), Task 7".</fix></finding>
<finding task="10"><quote>A `skills/*/scripts/*.py` file with a `__main__` guard carries a PEP 723 block that parses with `tomllib` and has `requires-python` and `dependencies`.</quote><plan>**DF6. Vendored scripts** are exempt from the two header rules through `VENDORED_SCRIPTS` (empty today); the invocation rule still applies to them.</plan><fix>R3.7 allows no exemption, so the plan should not add one silently. Either drop `VENDORED_SCRIPTS`, along with its test and constant, until a vendored script actually exists (YAGNI). Or bring the exemption to the owner as a spec amendment in Task 1 and log it as a decision.</fix></finding>
<finding task="2"><quote>Record the scenario, prompts, outputs, and verdicts in `specs/red-baseline-description-openings-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`, the house red-baseline format.</quote><plan>- The guidance is writing-skills' frontmatter bullets, Skill Discovery Optimization sections 1 and 2, the Token Efficiency section's `description` bullet and the checklist's description items, as they stood at `<sha>`, before any edit (`build_prompt.py`; prompt sha256 `<hash>`).</plan><fix>The record template keeps only a hash of the prompt and the 150-character prefix of each output. Add a `## Prompt` section that holds the full text of red-prompt.txt in a fence. Add a `## Outputs` section with each rep's full reply verbatim, VOID reps included. Use the same layout for the GREEN arm.</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>Every plan MUST start with this header: … ## Review Focus</quote><plan>## Global Constraints … ## Decisions</plan><fix>Add the required `## Review Focus` section, listing five uncovered input classes, each with a pinning test placed in its task. Candidates:
- a non-ASCII `compatibility` value near the cap;
- a SKILL.md with CRLF line endings, which `FRONTMATTER_RE` misses for the body warning;
- `from x import y` inside an `if TYPE_CHECKING:` block;
- an invocation with a quoted path containing spaces;
- a skill directory whose `LICENSE` copy is stale after a root license edit.</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>A plan more than about five times as long as the spec it implements is a transcript of the program, not a plan: cut it before you save it.</quote><plan>**Edit `build/check_frontmatter.py`: insert before the line `def check_skill(skill_dir: Path) -> list[str]:`:** … def check_script_headers(skill_dir: Path, vendored: frozenset[str] = VENDORED_SCRIPTS) -> list[str]: … (full function bodies throughout Tasks 3–12, plus the full helper scripts and the Planning record)</plan><fix>The plan is many times the spec's length and writes out function bodies that the signatures and tests already determine. Replace the bodies of these functions with their signatures, tests and one-line approach notes: `_check_value_shapes`, `_check_license`, `_check_invocation_parity`, `skill_body_warning`, `strict_violations`, `bundled_license_violations`, `required_imports`, `check_script_headers`, `resolve_bundled_script`, `bundled_invocations`, `check_invocations` and `_check_compatibility_names_uv`. Keep exact copy as it is: the spec text, the R3.5 sentence, the NOTICE/README/CLAUDE.md wording and the micro-test prompt. Condense the Planning record.</fix></finding>
</findings>
